2004B16.goal: Three unit circles, mutually tangent, sit inside a larger circle touching it. We want the large radius. The small centres form an equilateral triangle of side $2$.

tools.name: Circumradius
tools.why: For an equilateral triangle of side $s$.

tools.name: Internal tangency
tools.why: Distance to a small centre plus its radius.

check.q: What is the circumradius of an equilateral triangle with side $2$?

2004B16.bridge: Circumradius of the centre triangle, plus $1$.
2004B16.recognize: Equal circles packed in a circle: the centres form a regular polygon.

2004B17.goal: Jack is $\overline{ab}$, Bill is $\overline{ba}$; in $5$ years Jack is twice Bill. We want the age difference $9(a-b)$.

tools.name: Equation
tools.why: "In five years" adds $5$ to both.

tools.name: Digit constraint
tools.why: Leaves few solutions.

2004B17.bridge: Write the ages with digits and solve $8a=19b+5$.
2004B17.shortcut: The difference of reversed two-digit numbers is a multiple of $9$.
traps: Forgetting to add $5$ to both ages.
2004B17.recognize: Reversed-digit ages: set up with $10a+b$ and $10b+a$.

2004B18.goal: Right triangle $ACE$ ($12$-$16$-$20$, right angle at $C$) with $AB=3$, $CD=4$, $EF=5$ — each a quarter of its side. We want $\tfrac{[DBF]}{[ACE]}$. Subtract the three corner triangles.

tools.name: Corner triangle ratio
tools.why: Shared angle at $A$.

tools.name: Each corner
tools.why: One side is cut at $\tfrac14$, the other at $\tfrac34$.

2004B18.approach: Each corner triangle is $\tfrac{3}{16}$ of $[ACE]$. Three of them: $\tfrac9{16}$. Remaining: $\tfrac7{16}$.
2004B18.shortcut: Same cut fraction $t$ on all sides: inner triangle $=1-3t(1-t)$.
2004B18.recognize: Triangle inside a triangle via points on sides: subtract corner triangles.

2004B19.goal: $a_n=a_{n-3}+a_{n-2}-a_{n-1}$ starting $2001,2002,2003$. We want $a_{2004}$. Look at consecutive-pair sums.

tools.name: Pair sums
tools.why: Rearranging the rule.

tools.name: Even-index terms
tools.why: Even terms drop by $2$ each time.

2004B19.approach: Pair sums alternate $4003,4005$. So $a_n-a_{n-2}=\pm2$: even-index terms go $2002,2000,1998,\ldots$. $a_{2004}=2002-2\cdot1001=0$.
2004B19.shortcut: Compute $8$ terms and the two interleaved sequences are obvious.
2004B19.recognize: Odd recurrences: compute a few terms; look for interleaved arithmetic sequences.

2004B20.goal: Cevians $AD$ and $BE$ meet at $T$ with $\tfrac{AT}{DT}=3$ and $\tfrac{BT}{ET}=4$. We want $\tfrac{CD}{BD}$. Use mass points.

tools.name: Mass points
tools.why: $T$ balances each cevian.

tools.name: Masses add
tools.why: $D$ on $BC$, $E$ on $AC$.

check.why: The heavier end is closer to $D$.

2004B20.recognize: Two cevians with known division ratios: mass points.

2004B21.goal: $S$ is the union of the first $2004$ terms of $1,4,7,\ldots$ and $9,16,23,\ldots$. Count distinct elements: $4008$ minus the overlap.

tools.name: Common terms
tools.why: CRT; $16$ is the smallest that works.

2004B21.shortcut: The overlap is limited by the shorter range ($6010$).
2004B21.recognize: Unions of arithmetic progressions: CRT for the intersection, then inclusion–exclusion.

2004B22.goal: For the $5$-$12$-$13$ right triangle, find the distance between the incentre and circumcentre. Use coordinates.

tools.name: Circumcentre
tools.why: Right triangle (Thales).

tools.name: Inradius
tools.why: Right-triangle formula.

2004B22.approach: Right angle at $(0,0)$, legs along the axes to $(12,0)$ and $(0,5)$. Incentre $(2,2)$, circumcentre $(6,\tfrac52)$. Distance $\sqrt{16+\tfrac14}$.
traps: Placing the incentre at the centroid.
2004B22.recognize: Right-triangle centres: circumcentre at the hypotenuse midpoint, incentre at $(r,r)$.

2004B23.goal: Each face of a cube is red/blue at random. We want $P(\text{some placement has four same-coloured vertical faces})$. That means some "belt" of four faces (all faces except an opposite pair) is monochromatic.

tools.name: Case by colour counts
tools.fact: 6\text{ or }5\text{ of a colour: always works}
tools.why: Put the odd face on top.

tools.name: Four of a colour
tools.fact: \text{works only if the other two are opposite}
tools.why: They must be the top and bottom.

2004B23.approach: All one colour: $2$. Five–one: $2\cdot6=12$. Four–two with the two opposite: $2\cdot3=6$. Three–three never works. Total $20$ of $64$.

check.q: How many pairs of opposite faces does a cube have?

2004B23.bridge: Count colourings by how many faces share the majority colour.
2004B23.shortcut: Inclusion–exclusion over the $3$ belts gives the same $20$.
traps: Counting four–two with adjacent odd faces.
2004B23.recognize: Cube colourings with a placement condition: case on the colour counts.

2004B24.goal: $AB=7$, $AC=8$, $BC=9$; $D$ on the circumcircle with $AD$ bisecting $\angle A$. We want $\tfrac{AD}{CD}$. $D$ is the midpoint of arc $BC$, so $BD=CD$; use Ptolemy.

tools.name: Arc midpoint
tools.why: Equal inscribed angles $\angle BAD=\angle CAD$ subtend equal chords.

tools.name: Ptolemy's theorem
tools.why: Cyclic quadrilateral $ABDC$.

steps.title: Equal chords
steps.explain: $\angle BAD=\angle DAC$ subtend chords $BD$ and $DC$, so $BD=CD$.

2004B24.shortcut: In general $\tfrac{AD}{CD}=\tfrac{AB+AC}{BC}$ for the bisector to the arc midpoint.
traps: Using the bisector's intersection with $BC$ instead of the circle.
Ordering the quadrilateral wrongly in Ptolemy.
2004B24.recognize: Angle bisector extended to the circumcircle: arc midpoint, equal chords, Ptolemy.

2004B25.goal: A unit circle with diameter $AB$ is internally tangent to two radius-$2$ circles at $A$ and $B$. We want the area inside both big circles but outside the small one. The big circles are centred at $B$ and $A$.

tools.name: Big centres
tools.fact: \text{centre of the circle tangent at }A\text{ is }B
tools.why: It lies on line $AO$ at distance $2$ from $A$.

tools.name: Lens area
tools.why: Two radius-$2$ circles with centres $2$ apart meet at $120^\circ$ arcs.

2004B25.approach: Lens of circles centred at $A$ and $B$ (distance $2$): $\tfrac{8\pi}3-2\sqrt3$. The small circle lies inside the lens; subtract $\pi$.

steps.title: Lens
steps.explain: Intersection points $(0,\pm\sqrt3)$ with $A=(-1,0)$, $B=(1,0)$. Each segment: sector $\tfrac{4\pi}3$ minus triangle $\sqrt3$. Lens $=\tfrac{8\pi}3-2\sqrt3$.

check.q: What is the area of a $120^\circ$ sector of radius $2$?

2004B25.bridge: Lens area minus the small disk.
solution: Big circles are centred at $A$ and $B$, $2$ apart.
2004B25.shortcut: Radius $2$, centres $2$ apart: the classic $120^\circ$ lens.
traps: Placing the big centres at distance $1$ from $O$ on the same side.
Forgetting to subtract the small circle.
2004B25.recognize: Overlap of two equal circles: twice a circular segment.
